1	**Source ID**: [SRC-ISSUE-02]
2	
3	# Issue: otelhttp: Cannot record error for spans when producing new semantic convention (open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib#7254)
4	
5	**Canonical URL**: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/7254  
6	**Author**: XSAM  
7	**Created**: 2025-04-23T02:21:22Z · **Updated**: 2026-01-13T15:23:09Z  
8	**Collected**: 2026-07-14T14:35:41Z  
9	**State**: closed (completed)  
10	**Labels**: bug, area: instrumentation, instrumentation: otelhttp  
11	**Milestone**: v1.40.0
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Description
16	
17	### Description
18	
19	`otelhttp` only uses `span.RecordError(err)` when `errType` is not empty
20	
21	https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/blob/b8572491f2d143672581d1c51693c928d376dff8/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp/transport.go#L132-L140
22	
23	But `ErrorType` method never returns an empty attribute.
24	
25	https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/blob/b8572491f2d143672581d1c51693c928d376dff8/instrumentation/net/http/httptrace/otelhttptrace/internal/semconv/httpconv.go#L443-L458
26	
27	### Expected behavior
28	
29	I don't have a preference on whether we should record `error.type` with `exception.type` at the same time. But the comment and the logic here seem conflicted. 
30	
31	
32	## Discussion (15)
33	
34	**dmathieu** — 2025-04-23T08:03:12Z
35	
36	I don't know what was the intent there. But it feels like `ErroTypeOther` should be the case where we want to fallback to recording an error?
37	
38	---
39	
40	**XSAM** — 2025-04-23T16:07:50Z
41	
42	> But it feels like ErroTypeOther should be the case where we want to fallback to recording an error?
43	
44	I don't find a way to make it return `ErrorTypeOther`. In most cases, it returns `semconv.ErrorTypeKey.String("*errors.errorString")`.
45	
46	For instance, errors created by `errors.New()` like `driver.ErrBadConn`. The type is `*errors.errorString`.
47	
48	I know it is difficult (or impossible) to get this via reflect, but do you think returning `semconv.ErrorTypeKey.String("database/sql/driver.ErrBadConn")` is the ideal result for `driver.ErrBadConn`?
49	
50	> where we want to fallback to recording an error?
51	
52	I feel we should always make span recording the error, as this is the only way users can choose to record [`exception.message`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/4676c009fa6b8f4ed7d2321c991024373e77428e/docs/attributes-registry/exception.md#exception-message) and [`exception.stacktrace`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/4676c009fa6b8f4ed7d2321c991024373e77428e/docs/attributes-registry/exception.md#exception-stacktrace). While only know the error type does not seem to help a lot, these two attributes are very helpful when debugging.
53	
54	@open-telemetry/go-maintainers What do you think about this issue?
55	
56	---
57	
58	**XSAM** — 2025-04-24T18:26:30Z
59	
60	More information: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/exceptions/ (not in the semconv doc)
61	
62	The spec about exceptions says
63	
64	> An exception SHOULD be recorded as an Event on the span during which it occurred if and only if it remains unhandled **when the span ends and causes the span status to be set to ERROR**.
65	
66	It even has a pseudo code that sets the `error.type` attribute for spans and calls `recordException` at the same time.
67	
68	```java
69	Span span = myTracer.startSpan(/*...*/);
70	try {
71	  // Code that does the actual work which the Span represents
72	} catch (Throwable e) {
73	  span.recordException(e);
74	  span.setAttribute(AttributeKey.stringKey("error.type"), e.getClass().getCanonicalName())
75	  span.setStatus(StatusCode.ERROR, e.getMessage());
76	  throw e;
77	} finally {
78	  span.end();
79	}
80	```
81	
82	---
83	
84	So, a good start for us is to change the code from
85	
86	```go
87			// set error type attribute if the error is part of the predefined
88			// error types.
89			// otherwise, record it as an exception
90			if errType := t.semconv.ErrorType(err); errType.Valid() {
91				span.SetAttributes(errType)
92			} else {
93				span.RecordError(err)
94			}
95	
96			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())
97	```
98	
99	to
100	
101	```go
102			// ErrorType should always return a valid error.type` for error
103			span.SetAttributes(t.semconv.ErrorType(err))
104			span.RecordError(err)
105			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())
106	```
107	
108	---
109	
110	**pellared** — 2025-06-11T12:24:35Z
111	
112	What is the value of recording the error as event if the type is set as attribute and value (`err.Error()`) as status description?
113	
114	> An exception SHOULD be recorded as an Event on the span during which it occurred if and only if it remains unhandled when the span ends and causes the span status to be set to ERROR.
115	
116	I argue that error result is not an exception. For me a `panic` that was not being recovered is an unhandled exception. We already cover this part of this specification here:
117	
118	https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/bc531cb3f9ce9c328b12e473b6409784728dc608/sdk/trace/span.go#L465-L482
119	
120	Additionally see: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/general/recording-errors.md#recording-errors-on-spans
121	
122	Therefore, we should not call `span.RecordError(err)`.
123	
124	---
125	
126	**dashpole** — 2025-06-12T17:03:33Z
127	
128	@pellared does that mean span.RecordError should essentially never be called by instrumentation, since panic recovery is already handled by the SDK?
129	
130	Almost makes it seem like we should deprecate RecordError in the API, and document that End should handle recording exceptions for panics.
131	
132	---
133	
134	**pellared** — 2025-06-13T07:21:05Z
135	
136	My proposal is to not use `span.RecordError` for **terminating errors** per [recording errors on spans semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/general/recording-errors.md#recording-errors-on-spans).
137	
138	During the SIG meeting, it was also noted that `span.RecordError` captures a stack trace. However, since the stack trace reflects where the error was recorded, not where it originated, I don’t find it particularly valuable. Additionally, capturing and emitting a stack trace has a performance cost. In most languages with exception handling (such as Java or .NET), the stack trace is already included in the thrown exception so the cost of capturing the stack trace was already taken and the stack trace is taken in the place where the exception was thrown.
139	
140	> @pellared does that mean span.RecordError should essentially never be called by instrumentation, since panic recovery is already handled by the SDK? Almost makes it seem like we should deprecate RecordError in the API,
141	
142	I believe [`span.RecordError`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/trace/api.md#record-exception) remains valuable, particularly for **non-terminating errors**. A common use case is **retry logic**, where errors occur but don't immediately end the span. This is especially relevant in the context of **custom instrumentation**, where developers have full control and can explicitly record such intermediate errors.
143	
144	While instrumentation libraries typically just return errors, they could also benefit from `span.RecordError` if the underlying library provides hooks into retry or failure logic. In such cases, recording retry attempts as span events via `span.RecordError` gives users better visibility into transient issues **without prematurely ending the span**.
145	
146	For these reasons, I don’t think `span.RecordError` should be deprecated. It might be worth capturing these use cases in the [error recording semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/general/recording-errors.md) (cc @lmolkova).
147	
148	Side note: There is an OTEP https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/4333 that proposes to record exceptions/errors as log records instead of span events.
149	
150	>  and document that End should handle recording exceptions for panics.

## Status of `opentelemetry-go-contrib` #7254

**Closed as completed** on 2026-01-13 by `pellared`. Per the authoritative Work State, the task (`T002`) is done, but **no release is established** in the record.

### Current state
- **State**: `closed (completed)`; **Milestone**: `v1.40.0`; **Labels**: `bug`, `area: instrumentation`, `instrumentation: otelhttp` (`c2/opentelemetry/issues/opentelemetry-go-contrib-7254.md`)
- Work State `T002` is checked off: "Resolve otelhttp error-recording behavior for new semantic conventions. Closed as completed; release not established." (`c2/work-states/WS-05-contrib.md`)
- The v1.40.0 milestone itself is closed (169 closed / 0 open), but the Work State explicitly notes "No release Source after `v1.39.0` establishes delivery" (`c2/opentelemetry/milestones/milestone-14282228.md`, `c2/work-states/WS-05-contrib.md`)

### The problem
`otelhttp`'s transport only called `span.RecordError(err)` when `errType` was *invalid*, but `ErrorType` never returns an empty/invalid attribute — so the comment and the logic contradicted each other, and errors were effectively never recorded as exceptions. Reported by `XSAM` on 2025-04-23 (`c2/opentelemetry/issues/opentelemetry-go-contrib-7254.md`).

### How it was resolved (the substantive decision)
The discussion converged on **not** calling `RecordError` for terminating errors. `pellared` argued an error result is not an exception — unhandled panics are already covered by the SDK's `span.End`, and `RecordError`'s stack trace reflects where the error was *recorded*, not where it originated, at a performance cost. `XSAM` accepted this on 2025-08-05, agreeing the pattern should be:

```go
span.SetAttributes(semconv.ErrorType(err))
span.SetStatus(codes.Error, err.Error())
```

`RecordError` remains valuable for **non-terminating** errors (e.g. retry visibility in custom instrumentation), so no deprecation. `dashpole` conditioned agreement on the guidelines matching the current Development spec rather than getting ahead of it; `pellared` confirmed they would follow the in-Development semconv.

### Chronology
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 2025-04-23 | Opened by `XSAM` |
| 2025-06-16 | `pellared` spins off follow-ups: contrib `#7470`, go `#6903`/`#6904` |
| 2025-09-18 | Milestoned to `v1.39.0` by `MrAlias` |
| 2025-10-30 | SIG meeting: flagged as possibly the **only blocker** to otelhttp stabilization; Robert takes ownership to draft a clarification doc |
| 2025-11-03 | `pellared` states semconv "recording errors on spans" must go Stable before otelhttp v1 |
| 2025-12-04 | Demilestoned from `v1.39.0`, moved to `v1.40.0` |
| 2026-01-12 | Cross-referenced from PR `#8386` |
| 2026-01-13 | **Closed** by `pellared` |

(`c2/opentelemetry/issues/opentelemetry-go-contrib-7254.md`, `c2/opentelemetry/meeting-notes/entry-3479655348.md`)

### Caveats worth flagging
- **Delivery not confirmed.** PR `#8386` appears only as a cross-reference immediately before closure; the records contain no merge event for it and no release Source proving the fix shipped. The Work State lists "any release containing `#7254`" under *Next Update Needed*.
- **Stabilization link.** The 2025-10-30 SIG treated #7254 as the likely sole blocker for otelhttp stabilization, though the group also agreed bugs don't inherently block stabilization if fixes are non-breaking or properly versioned. The broader guideline work continues under contrib `#7470`, gated on the semconv error-recording doc moving from Development to Stable (`c2/opentelemetry/meeting-notes/entry-3479655348.md`).
